input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale: Two material failures against the fallback. (1) Section 4.1 (p0024) grants only a symmetric right — "terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other" — embedded in the automatic-renewal sentence, so it neither expressly gives the Company a convenience right nor confines HDI to the expiry of the then-current term (the "Such notice shall specify the date" sentence would let HDI choose any date 90+ days out). Operation 1 states both points in operative words: notice on the same ninety (90) days to the other, exercisable "by the Company for convenience at any time or by HDI only at the end of a term", which also removes any argument that the right is merely a non-renewal mechanic. (2) Section 4.2(a) (p0026) imposes on the Company alone a Termination Payment of half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, payable in eight quarterly instalments (p0029) with no reciprocal HDI payment (p0028) — roughly $600,000 on $2,000,000 of Net Sales against about $140,000 of three months' Section 3.1 fees. Operation 2 adds a three-month fee ceiling as prong (ii) of a "lesser of", retaining the original computation as prong (i) so the Company still owes nothing at or below $800,000 of trailing Net Sales and Section 4.2(b)'s zero-or-less netting stays operative; 4.2(c), the Termination Date definition and the renewal structure are untouched. Preferred is not claimed: notice stays at 90 rather than 30 days and no pro-rata refund is added, there being no prepaid fees under this revenue-share model. The residual point that 4.2(a) still bites on a termination for HDI's breach is outside this checklist and is raised in the comment only.

proposal.summary: State expressly that the Company may terminate for convenience at any time on 90 days' written notice and HDI only at the end of a term on the same notice, and cap the Termination Payment at three months of Section 3.1 fees as a ceiling on the existing calculation.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 4.1 now says expressly that the Company may terminate for convenience at any time on ninety (90) days' written notice, while HDI may terminate only at the end of a term on the same notice; the symmetric wording left both points to inference and read as a mere non-renewal right. In Section 4.2(a) we have capped the Termination Payment at three months of Section 3.1 fees as a ceiling on the existing calculation, so Section 4.2(b)'s netting outcome is preserved. We would also expect 4.2(a) not to bite where we terminate for HDI's breach, consistent with Section 1.6.

ops.oldText: for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other.
ops.newText: for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other, by the Company for convenience at any time or by HDI only at the end of a term.

ops.oldText: the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
ops.newText: the amount of which shall be the lesser of (i) the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, divided by two, and (ii) the payments due to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date.
